candidates.attacker_control: The untrusted script author fully controls both the default-value expression and the name/number of parameters, e.g. a script-level method `def f(x = <forbidden expression>) { ... }` or a closure `def c = { x = <forbidden expression> -> ... }`, and controls whether the parameter is omitted when invoking `f()` / `c()` (which forces evaluation of the default expression). No privileges beyond the ability to submit Groovy source are needed.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: I verified that all other script-visible constructs in this codebase do get rewritten: MethodCallExpression, StaticMethodCallExpression, MethodPointerExpression, ConstructorCallExpression, AttributeExpression, PropertyExpression, VariableExpression-as-property, BinaryExpression (assignments, array access, in, regex, comparisons, other operators), Prefix/PostfixExpression and CastExpression (SandboxTransformer lines 347-604). I confirmed fields are visited (lines 145-147), object initializer statements are visited (142-144), and constructors are rewritten via processConstructors (159-232), i.e. the omission is specific to parameter initial expressions and not a general pattern. I also considered that Groovy's own ClassCodeExpressionTransformer might transform defaults before/while the sandbox visitor runs; if it did, the sandbox's own visitor would not need to manually re-traverse closure bodies, but this could not be verified because the groovy 2.4.7 jar/sources are not in the snapshot.
candidates.impact: Sandbox escape / protection-mechanism bypass: script code inside default parameter values executes with no interceptor review, so any operation the sandbox's policy would deny (arbitrary method/static calls, constructors, property/attribute access) can be reached through a default value, defeating the library's core guarantee that 'every operation that can cause interactions with the external world gets intercepted' (SandboxTransformer javadoc lines 84-92; src/site/markdown/index.md lines 6-8).
candidates.prerequisites: A deployment that relies on this library to constrain untrusted Groovy (GroovyShell with SandboxTransformer + a GroovyInterceptor registered), and Groovy evaluating parameter default expressions when the argument is omitted. Groovy version is pinned to 2.4.7 in pom.xml (lines 84-89); whether org.codehaus.groovy.ast.ClassCodeExpressionTransformer.visitConstructorOrMethod in that version already transforms Parameter initial expressions could not be verified from this snapshot (see unverified).
candidates.root_cause: SandboxTransformer rewrites expressions into Checker.checked* calls only for AST nodes it traverses. When it handles parameters it only records names (ScopeTrackingClassCodeExpressionTransformer.declareVariable, lines 176-178) and never calls transform() on Parameter.getInitialExpression(). Method/constructor parameters are handled in ScopeTrackingClassCodeExpressionTransformer.visitMethod/withMethod (lines 39-58) and closure parameters in SandboxTransformer.VisitorImpl.innerTransform (lines 320-345), which visits only ce.getCode(). A grep for getInitialExpression over the whole repo returns no matches, so default-value expressions remain raw AST and are compiled by Groovy into ordinary, unchecked call sites instead of Checker calls; registered GroovyInterceptors never see them.
candidates.title: Default parameter values of methods/closures are never sandbox-transformed, bypassing Checker and all interceptors
candidates.trace: 1) SandboxTransformer.call (lines 130-148) walks methods, initializers and fields; methods go to ScopeTracking.visitMethod (lines 39-48), which only declares parameter names and delegates to ClassCodeExpressionTransformer. 2) Closure bodies are manually re-traversed in innerTransform because 'ClosureExpression.transformExpression doesn't visit the code inside' (lines 320-344); only ce.getCode() is visited and parameters are merely declared (lines 325-335). 3) Parameter.getInitialExpression() is never visited/transformed anywhere (search for getInitialExpression finds no occurrence), so any MethodCallExpression / ConstructorCallExpression / PropertyExpression / AttributeExpression written as a default value is never rewritten into Checker.checkedCall/checkedConstructor/checkedGetProperty. 4) Groovy expands default arguments into synthetic overloads at a later phase, compiling the un-transformed expression tree directly, so at execution time no Checker method runs and no GroovyInterceptor.on* callback is invoked, even though every other call in the script would be intercepted.
candidates.unverified: Cannot run Groovy 2.4.7 or inspect its ClassCodeExpressionTransformer/ClosureExpression source from this snapshot, so it is not runtime-confirmed that (a) parameter default expressions are left untransformed by the base transformer class, and (b) the compiled synthetic overload evaluates them through normal (unchecked) call sites. No test sources are present in the snapshot to corroborate. The finding should be validated by dynamically inspecting the AST/compiled output of a script defining `def f(x = <expr>) {}` under SandboxTransformer.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-693 Protection Mechanism Failure (sandbox interceptor bypass / incomplete AST instrumentation)

coverage_summary: All 22 files in the assigned snapshot were discovered; I read in full the security-relevant sources: GroovyInterceptor.java, GroovyValueFilter.java, SandboxTransformer.java, ScopeTrackingClassCodeExpressionTransformer.java, StackVariableSet.java, Checker.java, Ops.java, ClosureSupport.java, Super.java, SandboxedMethodClosure.java, all four InvokerChain classes, pom.xml, README.md, src/site/markdown/index.md and ast.sh. Only .gitignore, LICENSE.md and src/site/site.xml were not read (non-executable metadata). Search covered SECURITY-/JENKINS- markers, TODO comments, and getInitialExpression/Parameters usage. No test sources exist in the snapshot, so no tests were available to corroborate or refute behavior.
limitations: No precomputed source-relation index in B0; results are based on manual traversal of the 22 visible files.

The Groovy 2.4.7 library internals (ClassCodeExpressionTransformer, ClosureExpression.transformExpression, default-argument expansion) are not part of the snapshot and could not be inspected; the candidate depends on that external behavior.
No execution, compilation, or exploitability testing was performed, so the default-parameter-value bypass is a source-evidence-based lead, not a confirmed vulnerability.
Behavior may differ between plain GroovyShell use and Jenkins CPS-transformed usage (CpsScript/SerializableScript), which is only referenced in TRIVIAL_CONSTRUCTORS and not implemented here.

rejected_leads.lead: SandboxTransformer lines 490-496: `this.<name> = value` is returned as an untransformed BinaryExpression when clazz.getField(name) != null, skipping checkedSetProperty (and, because the returned node is not re-transformed, the LHS getter as well).
rejected_leads.reason: Real code-path skip, but confined to fields (including inherited public fields) of the sandboxed class itself; the comment explicitly deems it internal state, and no untrusted-data read/return to the environment is demonstrated, so security impact is weak compared with cand-1.

rejected_leads.lead: SandboxTransformer lines 512-516: LHS FieldExpression of an assignment is deliberately not intercepted ('not sure how we can intercept this, so skipping this for now'); FieldExpression is documented as mapping to direct GETSTATIC/SETSTATIC/GETFIELD/SETFIELD access.
rejected_leads.reason: Acknowledged-by-comment limitation and, like the previous lead, only directly affects field reads/writes rather than arbitrary method execution; exploitability via @CompileStatic/direct field bytecode could not be established from this snapshot.

rejected_leads.lead: prefixPostfixExp returns `whole` untransformed at line 667 when the atom is neither an array access, a local variable, nor a PropertyExpression (e.g. FieldExpression under static compilation), leaving `x++`/`--x` entirely outside Checker.
rejected_leads.reason: Fallthrough exists, but the reachable operand kinds are field/attribute-like l-values of the script's own object; no clear route to an unchecked external call or sensitive read was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Logical operators (`&&`, `||`) and `instanceof` are intentionally passed through untransformed (lines 538-543), so `asBoolean()` dispatch on a script-supplied object is not reported to interceptors.
rejected_leads.reason: This is upstream-intended behavior (Ops.isLogicalOperator), the operand's own code is still transformed, and the call is on an object the script already holds; no concrete policy bypass is shown.

summary: This snapshot is groovy-sandbox 1.20-SNAPSHOT (Jenkins CSP-compatible compile-time sandbox). I read all 22 source files (the small metadata files .gitignore/LICENSE/site.xml were only listed). The design is sound overall: method/static calls, constructors, property/attribute/array access, casts, prefix/postfix and binary operators are rewritten to Checker.* calls that dispatch through GroovyInterceptor (SandboxTransformer 306-607; Checker 47-620; invoker chains). One structural gap stands out with the strongest source evidence: default parameter values of methods, constructors, and closures are never passed through the transformer, so script-authored code placed there is compiled directly and never reaches Checker/GroovyInterceptor. I also identified several weaker/acknowledged gaps (this-field write skip, FieldExpression skip, prefix/postfix fallthrough) and rejected them as the primary finding.
